goal.mission: Understand how to consistently go viral on YouTube Shorts.
goal.why: My life changes when I can do this: more people see me, relationships, long-term money.
success: 2 of 3 posts reach 10K+ views (per three-post experiment)
goal.method: Run 3-post experiments. Experiment, reflect, research, experiment again.

method: Attention grabbing scene, that is clear, intelligible

experiments.title: Experiment 3
experiments.summary: Add a readable title in the first frame, plus a clear hook shot.
experiments.hypothesis: A big, quick-to-read title (about 0.2 seconds to land) plus an attention-grabbing, cohesive first shot will make the content easier to see and raise views.
method: White background, black text title card
Candidate titles: "Jerry will never forgive me for what I'm about to do..." / "Jerry forgive me for what I'm about to do..."
Keep the scene clear and comprehensible
Keep the context readable and quick

experiments.title: Reflections and research after Experiment 2
experiments.summary: Content engages once watched. The problem is getting people to see it: add context fast.
results: Felt more like a skit than a normal video
Notes and research made it better
Videos need a title giving context. Titles matter a lot on YouTube: must have one and it must be easy to see
You have about 0.2 seconds to show a big title
Sometimes the title plus the video is enough
Focus on making the first frame digestible
My content is engaging when people watch, but I need to make it easier for people to see it
next_steps: Make sure the context is readable and quick
Try title + hook + attention-grabbing, clear, cohesive shot (Experiment 3)

method: 16 seconds in the Roblox Dummy Engine
Funny or attention-grabbing scene, me relating casually as main subject
Scene is comprehensible and clear what's happening

shorts.concept: Dummy goes Hulk and throws another. I tell Jefe: "Are you mad? I ate the last slice of pizza."
I blow Jerry out of the flames and say he can go back to community college now.
I blow Hulk to space and he explodes. (An earlier idea was crossed out.)

results: Results invalidated because all posts were on a different platform/account
Can't use a different account again
notes: Felt like a skit. I was getting tired and not super into it, but it felt much clearer for the audience

experiments.title: Experiment 1
experiments.summary: Dummy-in-danger scenes. Spider did best. Refine and rerun.
experiments.hypothesis: A funny, attention-grabbing scene + a sound of exclamation + a moment or relatable line will make my post go viral. Target length 16–18 seconds.

shorts.concept: Dummy in spider pit. "Samantha forgot to wash the dishes."
Dummy with the shark. "Tom, can you even swim?" [concept names unclear in notes; trampoline also mentioned]
Dummy on the ship. "Joe invested in SpaceX." [notes also mention rocket explosion]

results: Spider did best. Assumption: it was eye-grabbing just before the climax

Trampoline did second best but didn't perform super well: the first second shows the dummy in the sky with no context, so it's easy to scroll. The first frame has to explain before the climax, with just enough time
Last place was the rocket explosion. Assumed it was too close to the climax and watchers didn't understand what was happening

do: Eye-grabbing scene before the climax (but not too close) that explains the clip
avoid: No context scene near, or too close to, the climax
Confusing scene where it's not clear what's happening

notes: Easily understood silly premise (a spider is easily understood, a figure launching into space not so much)
Needs a bit of build-up before the climax, enough to understand the concept
Side list, context unclear: hotel in NYC 3 days; say I'm staying with a friend; redo wardrobe (Uniqlo)
Experiment idea: grab dummy after growth and fly away with them

ai_insights.text: Treat the spider-did-best conclusions as hypotheses. One post per concept can't separate premise from luck.
Experiment 3: change only the title card, keep the scene the same, so the result is clean.
Log swipe-away rate for every short. Your first-frame idea should move that number most.
A title like "Jerry will never forgive me..." only gives context to people who already know Jerry.

checklist.text: Eye-grabbing scene before the climax (but not too close) that explains the clip
Scene is comprehensible and it's clear what's happening
Funny or attention-grabbing scene with me relating casually as the main subject
A title that gives context and is easy to see (about 0.2 seconds to land)
Build up before the climax, enough to understand the concept.
Easily understood silly premise (a spider is, a figure launching into space isn't)
Notes and research done before making it
Context that is readable and quick (white background, black text)
Me being 100% there, thinking about how the audience understands and enjoys it
